newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH FINANCE MINISTRY TO EXPAND MONEY MARKET ROLE.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH FINANCE MINISTRY TO EXPAND MONEY MARKET ROLE.

text.p: The Agency of the Dutch Ministry of Finance will become a more significant money market participant from January 1, 1997, the Agency said on Wednesday.

The Agency is already able to raise liquidity through its Dutch Treasury Certificates programme (DTCs), the short-term borrowing programme of the Dutch government, and it is allowed to take in call money if the market has ample liquidity.
From January, the Agency will also be able to buy-back DTCs and its flexibility to put out money will increase if the parties involved come to an agreement.
"Not all details are clear yet, but the overall idea is there," an Agency source said.
The Agency said it would become a big player along with ABN AMRO, ING and several other money market participants.
The reform fits in with changes in the Dutch market as the Netherlands heads toward European Economic and Monetary Union, which is expected to be launched in January, 1999.
But the Agency said the Dutch central bank would remain responsible for monetary policy, with the Agency administering the Treasury.
